identity.title: PHANGS-JWST First Results: Variations in PAH Fraction as a Function of ISM Phase and Metallicity

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present maps tracing the fraction of dust in the form of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) in IC 5332, NGC 628, NGC 1365, and NGC 7496 from JWST/MIRI observations.

We use 12CO (2-1)“broad” moment 0 maps and corresponding error maps from the PHANGS-ALMA survey combining 12m+7m+Total Power (cite: PHANGSALMA2021Pipeline; PHANGSALMA2021Survey), to trace molecular gas, at ~ 1'' (~ 40 - 90 pc in our sample) resolution.

question.value: How does the PAH fraction vary as a function of ISM phase (ionized, neutral, molecular) and metallicity across nearby galaxy disks?

evidence.quote: In this Letter, we investigate the variations of the PAH fraction traced by a combination of JWST/MIRI filters across the full disk of four nearby galaxies, IC 5332, NGC 628, NGC 1365, and NGC 7496.

analysis_steps.goal: Convolve imaging and ancillary maps to common angular resolution

method.value: Convolve MIRI F770W, F1130W, and F2100W filter maps to 1'' resolution using theoretical PSFs from WEBBPSF and kernels constructed following Aniano et al. (2011); convolve ancillary maps with resolution lower than 1'' to 1'' and reproject H I maps to MIRI grid.

evidence.quote: We convolve all three filter maps to 1'' resolution, which is larger than the full-width at half-maximum of the F2100W filter (0.67''). The convolution kernels were computed using the theoretical PSFs of each filter provided by the WEBBPSF (cite: WebbPSF)

evidence.quote: Based on the observed flatness of the atomic gas surface density over the inner parts of galaxy disks... we assume that the atomic gas has a flat distribution with Sigma_HI = 8 M_sun pc^-2 (including helium).

analysis_steps.goal: Compute PAH fraction proxy and analyze trends with ISM phase and metallicity

method.value: Calculate R_PAH = (F770W + F1130W) / F2100W pixel-by-pixel after S/N thresholding (S/N > 3) and AGN masking; measure radial profiles, trends with I_Halpha / Sigma_(HI + H2), molecular gas fraction, and environment

evidence.quote: Here, we use the JWST/MIRI R_PAH = (F770W+F1130W)/F2100W ratio as a proxy for the PAH fraction.
We remove pixels with signal-to-noise S/N <= 3 in all MIRI bands, with background noise values of 0.05, 0.05, and 0.1 MJy sr^-1.

key_parameters.value: S/N > 3 threshold; background noise 0.05, 0.05, 0.1 MJy sr^-1 for F770W, F1130W, F2100W

evidence.quote: We remove pixels with signal-to-noise S/N <= 3 in all MIRI bands, with background noise values of 0.05, 0.05, and 0.1 MJy sr^-1.

assumptions.value: F2100W filter is dominated by small, hot dust grains and free from PAH contribution

evidence.quote: We assume the F2100W filter is free from contribution from PAHs and is instead dominated by small, hot dust grains

used_for.value: Computing theoretical PSFs for MIRI convolution kernels and AGN PSF masking

evidence.quote: The convolution kernels were computed using the theoretical PSFs of each filter provided by the WEBBPSF (cite: WebbPSF)
This is done using the WEBBPSF package (cite: WebbPSF), and centering the F2100W PSF on the central coordinates of each target.
The PHANGS-JWST team used the STScI Calibration pipeline 1.7.1 for NIRCam and 1.7.0 for MIRI, and Calibration Reference Data context number 0968 for both instruments.

results_numeric.quantity: PAH fraction breakdown threshold in I_Halpha / Sigma_(HI + H2)

evidence.quote: We use CO+Hi+Halpha to trace the interstellar gas phase and find that the PAH fraction decreases above a value of I_Halpha/Sigma_HI+H2 ~ 10^37.5 erg s^-1 kpc^-2 (M_odot pc^-2)^-1, in all four galaxies.

findings_qualitative.value: R_PAH shows clear depressions within H II regions traced by MUSE Halpha.

evidence.quote: In all cases, it appears that R_PAH shows clear depressions within H II regions, though NGC 628 and NGC 7496 show this contrast most clearly.

findings_qualitative.value: PAH fraction decreases with increasing galactocentric radius, tracking metallicity gradients.

evidence.quote: All galaxies show an overall decreasing trend with radius.

Radial profiles also show a decreasing PAH fraction with increasing radius, correlated with lower metallicity, in line with previous results showing a strong metallicity dependence to the PAH fraction.

findings_qualitative.value: The PAH fraction remains relatively constant across morphological environments with only slight variations (highest in bars and interarms, lower in spiral arms, centers, and disks).

evidence.loc: 3.2 Variation of PAH fraction with ISM environment
evidence.quote: In this panel, it appears that there is no striking differences between environments, again showing minimal variations of a few tens of percent, for individual galaxies.

claims.hypothesis: The PAH fraction varies with ISM phase and drops in ionized gas-dominated environments due to PAH destruction.
claims.experiment: Compare R_PAH = (F770W + F1130W)/F2100W from JWST/MIRI against I_Halpha / Sigma_(HI + H2) derived from MUSE Halpha and PHANGS-ALMA CO + 21 cm H I data.
claims.result: R_PAH remains flat until I_Halpha / Sigma_(HI + H2) reaches ~ 10^37.5 erg s^-1 kpc^-2 (M_sun pc^-2)^-1, above which it declines sharply across all four galaxies.
claims.finding: The process of PAH destruction in ionized gas operates similarly across diverse galactic targets at a common ionized-to-total gas threshold.

evidence.quote: We use CO+Hi+Halpha to trace the interstellar gas phase and find that the PAH fraction decreases above a value of I_Halpha/Sigma_HI+H2 ~ 10^37.5 erg s^-1 kpc^-2 (M_odot pc^-2)^-1, in all four galaxies.
Our results suggest that the process of PAH destruction in ionized gas operates similarly across the four targets.

claims.hypothesis: The PAH fraction correlates strongly with local and global metallicity.
claims.experiment: Trace R_PAH against radial distance r/r_25 and gas-phase 12+log(O/H) maps derived from MUSE H II regions.
claims.result: Global offsets in mean R_PAH correspond to average galaxy metallicity, and radial gradients show lower R_PAH at larger radii / lower metallicity.
claims.finding: Global metallicity sets the average PAH abundance in the neutral/diffuse ISM, though moderate local metallicity variations have secondary effects compared to ionized gas destruction.

evidence.loc: 3.2 Variation of PAH fraction with ISM environment
evidence.quote: This implies that while the average metallicity of each galaxy seems to influence the PAH fraction, the moderate local metallicity variations are not having a large effect on R_PAH.

why_this_data.value: MIRI F770W and F1130W trace ionized and neutral PAH emission respectively, while F2100W traces small hot dust continuum, allowing high-resolution mapping of the PAH fraction.

evidence.quote: The MIRI F770W and F1130W filters provide coverage of two of the most prominent PAH features at 7.7um and 11.3um, while the F2100W filter lends a useful comparison, tracing emission from larger dust grains

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Using Voronoi binning instead of pixel-by-pixel analysis

evidence.loc: 3.2 Variation of PAH fraction with ISM environment
evidence.quote: It will also be possible to test a Voronoï binning, to check whether the trends seen in Figure 2 would be significantly pulled down by taking into account more low-S/N pixels.

limitations_admitted.value: Lack of high-resolution H I mapping for IC 5332 and NGC 1365 required assuming a constant Sigma_HI = 8 M_sun pc^-2.

evidence.quote: We lack resolved 21 cm mapping for IC 5332 and NGC 1365. Based on the observed flatness of the atomic gas surface density over the inner parts of galaxy disks... we assume that the atomic gas has a flat distribution with Sigma_HI = 8 M_sun pc^-2

limitations_admitted.value: Central saturation and artifacts from active galactic nuclei in NGC 1365 and NGC 7496 required masking.

evidence.quote: In NGC 1365 and NGC 7496, we mask pixels in the center due to IR brightness of the active galactic nuclei (AGN), which saturate the signal mostly in the F2100W band.

reproducibility.score_reason: The paper uses published science products from the PHANGS-ALMA, PHANGS-MUSE, and PHANGS-JWST surveys. Key processing choices (convolution to 1'', conversion factors, S/N clipping) are documented, but some manual masking was performed by hand.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: ALMA data play a supporting role providing CO moment 0 maps for molecular gas surface densities; the primary observational advance is JWST/MIRI imaging.
